## Script Summary 
This script relies on `02_PanCancer-RenderReport-RNAseq.Rmd` to provide input (TCGA project to perform analysis on) and covariates
that were dynamically determined as part of meta data harmonization. 

This script: 

- Utilizes processed SummarizedExperiment RNAseq RDS file

- Performs differential gene expression (DGE) analysis using `DESeq2` to 
identify genes whose expression is associated with age controlling for covariates

- Performs Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) on the `DESeq2` results using `fgsea` package

- Performs Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA) on our RNAseq data using the `GSVA` package

- Regress GSVA results against age and covariates to identify gene sets whose activity is related to age 



```{r file paths}
se_directory <- file.path(PATH, "data/RNAseq/processed_SummarizedExperiments/")

output_dir_dge <- file.path(PATH,"results/RNAseq/DGE_analysis/")
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
create_reactable_table <- function(se, covariate_name) {
  if (!is.null(colData(se)[[covariate_name]])) {
    # Generate frequency table
    freq_table <- table(colData(se)[[covariate_name]])
    
    # Convert to data frame for reactable
    df <- as.data.frame(freq_table)
    names(df) <- c(covariate_name, "Count")
    
    # Create reactable
    reactable::reactable(df, highlight = TRUE)
  } else {
    cat(paste0("Covariate '", covariate_name, "' not found.\n"))
  }
}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
reactable_pretty <- function(results) {
 results <- results %>% mutate(across(where(~is.numeric(.) && any(. %% 1 != 0, na.rm = TRUE)), ~signif(., digits = 3)))
 reactable::reactable(results,searchable = TRUE,resizable = TRUE)
}
```

## Covariate Preparation 
We dynamically determine the covariates to include in a previous script ("metadata/scripts/05_Covariates.Rmd).
This script utilizes those covariates to create a design matrix for regression analysis `DESeq2`.
```{r Prepare Covariates }
# Start with a basic model including only the age variable
model_formula <- "~ Age"

# Remove samples with missing age
se <- se[, !is.na(se$Age)]

# Include purity only if selected_cancer_type is not "TCGA-LAML"
if (include_purity) {
  model_formula <- paste(model_formula, "+ purity")
  # Remove samples with missing purity
  se <- se[, !is.na(se$purity)]
}

# Dynamically add covariates and filter SE based on parameters
if (include_gender) {
  model_formula <- paste(model_formula, "+ gender")
  #Drop NA gender samples
  se <- se[,!is.na(se$gender)]
  create_reactable_table(se, "gender")
  }

if (include_race) {
  
  model_formula <- paste(model_formula, "+ race")
  #Drop NA race samples
  se <- se[,!is.na(se$race)]
  
  races_to_keep <- strsplit(as.character(races_to_include), ",\\s*")[[1]]
  #print(paste0("Only keeping samples in these racial categories: ", races_to_include))
  se <- se[, se$race %in% races_to_keep]
  create_reactable_table(se, "race")

}

if (include_subtype) {
  model_formula <- paste(model_formula, "+ subtype_selected")
  #Drop NA tumor subtypes samples
  se <- se[,!is.na(se$subtype_selected)]
  create_reactable_table(se, "subtype_selected")
}

if (include_hpv) {
    #drop HPV positive samples (should be for HNSC only as of now)
    se <- se[, !is.na(se$HPV.status) & se$HPV.status == "Negative"]
    create_reactable_table(se, "HPV.status")
}

# Convert model formula to a formula object
model_formula <- as.formula(model_formula)

# Print model being used 
# Here we use deparse to convert the formula to a string
model_formula_str <- deparse(model_formula)
paste0("Model Formula: ", model_formula_str)
```


```{r}
# Prepare the design matrix 
design <- model.matrix(model_formula, data = colData(se))
head(unique(design))
```

```{r check-samples, echo=FALSE}

num_samples <- ncol(se)

# Print the number of samples

# Check if the number of samples is less than 50
if (num_samples < 50) {
  # Stop the R Markdown rendering with a custom message
  stop("Less than 50 samples remaining. Analysis requires 50 samples.")
}
```

## DEseq2
Here, we  perform differential gene expression analysis using the `DESeq2` package. Note that we do not need to apply explicit normalization, as this is handled internally by the `DESeq()` function: 

This function performs a default analysis through the steps:

- estimation of size factors: estimateSizeFactors

- estimation of dispersion: estimateDispersions

- Negative Binomial GLM fitting and Wald statistics: nbinomWaldTest

Some rows have missing p-values. Why? some values in the results table can be set to NA for one of the following reasons:

- If within a row, all samples have zero counts, the baseMean column will be zero, and the log2 fold change estimates, p value and adjusted p value will all be set to NA. 

- If a row contains a sample with an extreme count outlier then the p value and adjusted p value will be set to NA. These outlier counts are detected by Cook’s distance

- If a row is filtered by automatic independent filtering, for having a low mean normalized count, then only the adjusted p value will be set to NA. Description and customization of independent filtering is described below

### Run DESeq2
Here we run `DESeq` with the default parameters and created model formula. 
```{r deseq2 analysis}
print(model_formula)

# Extract the filtered counts
counts_filtered <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se,"unstranded")

# Build the DESeq2 dataset object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts_filtered,
                              colData = colData(se),
                              design = model_formula)

# Run the DESeq2 pipeline
dds <- DESeq(dds, parallel = TRUE)
```

### Retrieve Results
Next, we retrieve our analysis results.

First, we retrieve our age-regression results including internal filtering by `DESeq2` using the `results()` function. This internal filtering essentially maximizes the number of significant differentially expressed genes by excluding some genes when calculating adjusted p-values. We utilize this report the number of significant DEGs for the cancer type. 
See more information here: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html#indfilt

Second, we retrieve the unfiltered results (results for ALL genes included in our analysis) with and without shrunken logFC values using the `DESeq2::lfcShrink()` function. The unfiltered, unshrunken results will be used perform gene set enrichment analysis using ALL available gene information. The shrunked results are saved for potential downstream analysis and visualization, but are not utilized in this workflow.  

We also save all versions of these results.
```{r}
# Get filtered results (default DESeq2 filtering)
results_filtered <- results(dds, name = "Age")  # Automatically applies independent filtering
results_filtered_df <- as.data.frame(results_filtered) %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj) & !is.na(log2FoldChange))  # Filter rows with missing values

# Save filtered, non-shrunken results
saveRDS(results_filtered_df, paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_filtered_DESeq2_results.rds"))
write.csv(results_filtered_df, gzfile(paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_filtered_DESeq2_results.csv.gz")))

# Save filtered, non-shrunken results
results_unfiltered <- results(dds, name = "Age", independentFiltering = FALSE)
saveRDS(results_unfiltered, paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_unfiltered_DESeq2_results.rds"))
write.csv(results_unfiltered, gzfile(paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_unfiltered_DESeq2_results.csv.gz")))

# Shrink log2 fold changes for unfiltered results
results_unfiltered_df <- as.data.frame(results_unfiltered)
results_shrunken <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "Age", type = "apeglm")
results_shrunken_df <- as.data.frame(results_shrunken)

# Save unfiltered, shrunken results
saveRDS(results_shrunken_df, paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_unfiltered_shrunken_DESeq2_results.rds"))
write.csv(results_shrunken_df, gzfile(paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_unfiltered_shrunken_DESeq2_results.csv.gz")))


# reactable of filtered results
reactable_pretty(as.data.frame(results_filtered_df))
```


### Summary Table
```{r summary deseq2}
# Summary Table for Filtered Results
summary_stats <- results_filtered_df %>%
  mutate(direction = ifelse(log2FoldChange > 0, "Up", "Down")) %>%
  summarise(
    Total = n(),
    Q_Value_0.05 = sum(padj <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q_Value_0.025 = sum(padj <= 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q_Value_0.01 = sum(padj <= 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    IncreasedExp_with_Age = sum(padj <= 0.05 & direction == "Up", na.rm = TRUE),
    DecreasedExp_with_Age = sum(padj <= 0.05 & direction == "Down", na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Print the summary table
reactable_pretty(summary_stats)
```

### Volcano Plot
This volcano plot visualizes the FILTERED results of our age-regression analysis with `DESeq2`.
```{r volc dseq2}
results_filtered_df$gene <- rownames(results_filtered_df)

min_diff <- 0  # Adjust this threshold as per your requirement
max_fdr <- 0.05
dat <- results_filtered_df |> 
  dplyr::mutate(gene_type = case_when(
    log2FoldChange >  min_diff & padj <= max_fdr ~ "up",
    log2FoldChange < -min_diff & padj <= max_fdr ~ "dn",
    .default = "ns"))


# Using dplyr to remove NAs from specific columns
dat_cleaned <- dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj) & !is.na(log2FoldChange))

# Now you can proceed with your plotting or further analysis
print(ggplot_volcano(
  dat = dat_cleaned,
  xaxis = "log2FoldChange",
  yaxis = "padj",
  gene_label = "gene",
  xlab = "log2FoldChange",
  title = "DESeq2 Volcano Plot",
  yintercept = max_fdr,
  xintercept = c(-min_diff, min_diff),
  sig_il_genes = TRUE,
  up_il_genes = TRUE,
  dn_il_genes = TRUE,
  top_n = 3
))
```

## GSEA 
Here we use `fgsea` to perform a gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) on the HALLMARK gene sets. 

### Rank Genes by Wald-Statistic
First we rank the genes from largest to smallest wald statistic from `DESeq2`, including ALL analyzed genes (unfiltered). 
```{r}
HALLMARK <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H") %>%
  split(x = .$gene_symbol, f = .$gs_name)

# Rank genes by shrunken log2 fold changes
ranks <- setNames(results_unfiltered_df$stat, rownames(results_unfiltered_df))
ranks <- ranks[!is.na(ranks)]  # Remove NAs
ranks <- sort(ranks, decreasing = TRUE)

cat("First 5 genes in ranked list: " ,head(names(ranks), 5))
cat("Length of ranked list: " , length(ranks))
```

### Results {.tabset}
```{r}
# Run fgsea
fgsea_results <- fgsea::fgsea(
  pathways = HALLMARK,
  stats = ranks
)

# Sort results by NES
fgsea_results <- fgsea_results[order(fgsea_results$NES, decreasing = TRUE), ]

# Save results
output_path_gsea <- file.path(PATH, "results/RNAseq/GSEA/fgsea/", selected_cancer_type)
if (!dir.exists(output_path_gsea)) {
  dir.create(output_path_gsea, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Flatten results
fgsea_results_flat <- fgsea_results
fgsea_results_flat$leadingEdge <- sapply(fgsea_results_flat$leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";")

# Save results as CSV
write.csv(fgsea_results_flat, file = file.path(output_path_gsea, "fgsea_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save as RDS for full structure preservation
saveRDS(fgsea_results, file = file.path(output_path_gsea, "fgsea_results.rds"))
```

#### Horizontal Bar Plot
```{r}
# Filter significant results (FDR < 0.05)
significant_results <- fgsea_results[fgsea_results$padj < 0.05, ]
# Horizontal bar plot of significant pathways sorted by NES with updated legend
if (nrow(significant_results) > 0) {
  ggplot(significant_results, aes(reorder(pathway, NES), NES)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = NES > 0)) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      x = "Pathway",
      y = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)",
      title = "Significant Pathways (FDR < 0.05)",
      fill = "Association with Age"  # Update legend title
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "blue"),  # Assign colors to TRUE/FALSE
      labels = c("FALSE" = "Negative", "TRUE" = "Positive")  # Update legend labels
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
} else {
  cat("No significant pathways (FDR < 0.05) found.\n")
}

```

#### Results Table
```{r}
fgsea_results_table <- fgsea_results %>% mutate(across(where(~is.numeric(.) && any(. %% 1 != 0, na.rm = TRUE)), ~signif(., digits = 3)))

reactable_pretty(fgsea_results_table)
```

#### Enrichment Plots
```{r}
# Plot enrichment for all significant pathways
if (nrow(significant_results) > 0) {
  plots <- list()  # Create a list to store the plots
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(significant_results))) {
    pathway_name <- significant_results$pathway[i]
    plot <- fgsea::plotEnrichment(
      pathway = HALLMARK[[pathway_name]],
      stats = ranks
    ) +
      labs(title = paste("Enrichment Plot:", pathway_name)) +
      theme_minimal()
    print(plot)  # Display the plot in the R Markdown output
    plots[[pathway_name]] <- plot  # Save the plot in the list

```

## GSEA Summary
```{r}
# Define the significance threshold
significant_threshold <- 0.05

# Determine significant pathways
fgsea_results$Significant <- fgsea_results$padj < significant_threshold

# Count significant pathways with increasing and decreasing NES
increasing_activity <- sum(fgsea_results$Significant & fgsea_results$NES > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
decreasing_activity <- sum(fgsea_results$Significant & fgsea_results$NES < 0, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a summary table
significance_summary <- data.frame(
  Increasing_Activity_Sig = increasing_activity,
  Decreasing_Activity_Sig = decreasing_activity
)

# Display summary in the report
reactable_pretty(as.data.frame(significance_summary))
```

## Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA)
GSVA is used here to assess the activity of the 50 HALLMARK gene sets across all cancer samples based on RNA sequencing. This essentially assigns a score for each cancer quantifying the activity of each gene set. We can then regress each cancer's GSVA score against age to identify if the biological process activity increases or decreases with age in each cancer. 


### GSVA Calculation

**Procedure**:

For each cancer type:

- **Data Preparation**: Use RNAseq data from all samples.

- **GSVA Computation**: Using the Gaussian kernel for continuity in expression data, gene set variation "scores" are calculated to represent the relative enrichment of the gene set in each sample.

### Gene Sets
We then use the `msigdbr` package to get the list of genes included in the 50 hallmark gene sets. We also print a table showing the # of genes we have available for each gene set. 

```{r}
cpm_data <- assay(se, "DESeq2_log")

# Load hallmark gene sets
hallmark_sets <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H")
hallmark_sets <- split(hallmark_sets$gene_symbol, hallmark_sets$gs_name)

# Assuming cpm_data is your expression matrix and hallmark_sets is your list of gene sets

# Extract gene names from expression data
genes_in_data <- rownames(cpm_data)

# Calculate the number of genes in each set and the number available in your data
gene_presence_table <- sapply(hallmark_sets, function(gene_set) {
  total_genes <- length(gene_set)
  genes_present <- sum(gene_set %in% genes_in_data)
  c(Total_Genes = total_genes, Genes_Present = genes_present)
})

# Convert to a data frame for better readability and display
gene_presence_df <- as.data.frame(t(gene_presence_table), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rownames(gene_presence_df) <- names(hallmark_sets)

# Optionally, add names for clarity
colnames(gene_presence_df) <- c("Total Genes in Set", "# of Genes Present in Data")

# Display the table using reactable for an interactive view
reactable_pretty(gene_presence_df)
```

### Run GSVA
Finally, lets run GSVA on the hallmark sets and save the results. We use the `DESeq2` normalized counts. 
```{r GSVA}
param <- GSVA::gsvaParam(exprData = cpm_data, geneSets = hallmark_sets,kcdf="Gaussian", maxDiff = TRUE, absRanking = FALSE)
gsva_res <- GSVA::gsva(param, verbose = FALSE)

# Optionally save the results
gsva_path <- file.path(PATH, "data/RNAseq/GSVA/", paste0(selected_cancer_type,"_GSVA_HALLMARK.rds"))
saveRDS(gsva_res, gsva_path)

csv_path <- file.path(PATH, "data/RNAseq/GSVA/", paste0(selected_cancer_type, "_GSVA_HALLMARK.csv.gz"))
write.csv(gsva_res, gzfile(csv_path), row.names = TRUE)
```

## GSVA Regression
Now we regress our GSVA scores against Age and the dynamically determined covariates to identify which biological processes are correlated with increasing age.

### Data Prep
Here we prepare the GSVA score for regression, merging it with our metadata. 
```{r}
# Assuming gsva_res is a matrix with gene sets as rows and samples as columns
# Convert GSVA results to a data frame and transpose
gsva_df <- as.data.frame(t(gsva_res))
# Set column names to gene set names
colnames(gsva_df) <- rownames(gsva_res)
# Add a column for Sample IDs, assuming column names of the matrix are Sample IDs
gsva_df$SampleID <- colnames(gsva_res)

# Load Metadata from SummarizedExperiment object
metadata <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)

# Merge GSVA scores with metadata
combined_data <- merge(gsva_df, metadata, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "submitter_id", all.x = TRUE)

reactable_pretty(as.data.frame(combined_data))
```


### Regression
Here we perform regression per gene set. 
```{r}
# Running the regressions using the prepared model formula
results_list <- lapply(names(hallmark_sets), function(pathway) {
  # Construct the full formula by inserting the pathway as the response variable
  full_formula_str <- paste(pathway, deparse(model_formula))
  full_formula <- as.formula(full_formula_str)  # Converts the string to a formula
  
  # Run the linear model
  lm_result <- lm(full_formula, data = combined_data)
  
  # Return the summary of the linear model
  summary(lm_result)
})

names(results_list) <- names(hallmark_sets)
```


### GSVA Regression : Age Results
Finally, we summarize our results for the regression of the GSVA scores per gene set, isolating the impact of Age. We include various linear regression metrics for each gene set.

We also summarize the # of gene sets that are upregulated/downregulated with age, using the regression coefficent (>0 = increasing activity with age, <0 decreasing) and the adjusted p-value (BH correction. )
```{r}
# Initialize vectors to store results
estimates <- numeric(length(results_list))
std_errors <- numeric(length(results_list))
t_values <- numeric(length(results_list))
p_values <- numeric(length(results_list))
pathway_names <- names(results_list)

# Extract coefficients and p-values
for (i in seq_along(results_list)) {
  x <- results_list[[i]]
  coef_summary <- x$coefficients
  if (!is.null(coef_summary) && "Age" %in% rownames(coef_summary)) {
    estimates[i] <- coef_summary["Age", "Estimate"]
    std_errors[i] <- coef_summary["Age", "Std. Error"]
    t_values[i] <- coef_summary["Age", "t value"]
    p_values[i] <- coef_summary["Age", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  } else {
    estimates[i] <- NA
    std_errors[i] <- NA
    t_values[i] <- NA
    p_values[i] <- NA
  }
}

# Adjust p-values
adj_p_values <- p.adjust(p_values, method = "BH")

# Create summary table
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Pathway = pathway_names,
  Estimate = estimates,
  Std.Error = std_errors,
  t.value = t_values,
  P_val = p_values,
  Adj.P_val = adj_p_values,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Set row names to pathway names
rownames(summary_table) <- pathway_names
```


```{r}
sum_path <- file.path(PATH, "results/RNAseq/GSVA/", paste0(selected_cancer_type,"_GSVA_HALLMARK_regression.rds"))
saveRDS(summary_table, sum_path)

# Display summary table
summary_table_r <- summary_table %>% mutate(across(where(~is.numeric(.) && any(. %% 1 != 0, na.rm = TRUE)), ~signif(., digits = 3)))
reactable::reactable(as.data.frame(summary_table_r), searchable = TRUE, resizable = TRUE)

## Summary of Significantly Correlated Gene Sets
# Determine significance based on adjusted p-values
significant_threshold <- 0.05
summary_table$Significant <- with(summary_table, Adj.P_val < significant_threshold & !is.na(Adj.P_val))

# Count of significant gene sets increasing and decreasing activity with age
increasing_activity <- sum(summary_table$Significant & summary_table$Estimate > 0)
decreasing_activity <- sum(summary_table$Significant & summary_table$Estimate < 0)

# Create summary table of significant counts
significance_summary <- data.frame(
  Increasing_Activity_Sig = increasing_activity,
  Decreasing_Activity_Sig = decreasing_activity
)

# Display significance summary
reactable_pretty(as.data.frame(significance_summary))
```
